title: Roman doctors: Becanus—justify three ways in Scripture
source_text: XVII. Porro Doctores Ecclesiae Romanae communi consensu fatentur justificationem omnibus istis modis in Scriptura sacra sumi: neque justificari significare solum, vel justitiam acquirere, vel in justitia crescere: sed frequenter etiam declarari, vel agnosci justum. Id videre est apud Becanum Jesuitam in Summa Theol. tom. 2. tract. 4. cap. 3. q. 1. Justificare in sacra Scriptura tripliciter, inquit, usurpatur. Primo ut sit idem, quod justum facere, ut Rom. 4. 5. Credenti in eum qui justificat impium. Secundo ut sit idem quod justiorem facere, ut Jacob. 2. 24. Videtis quoniam ex operibus justificatur homo, & non ex fide tantum. Et Apoc. 22. 11. Qui justus est justificetur adhuc. Tertio ut sit idem quod declarare, seu pronunciare aliquem justum, ut Prov. 17. 15. Qui justificat impium, & qui condemnat justum, abominabilis est uterque apud Deum. Hinc fit ut justificatio sumatur etiam tribus modis. Primo pro acquisitione justitiae. Is enim quem Deus justificat, id est, justum facit, dicitur acquirere justitiam. Secundo pro augmento justitiae. Cum enim justitia latitudinem habeat, is qui semel justitiam nactus est, potest in ea crescere & proficere. Tertio pro declaratione justitiae. Nam qui antea sanctus, aut etiam reus esset injustitiae, potest pronunciari & declarari tanquam justus, etiamsi justus non sit.
pass_a_gloss: Further, the Doctors of the Roman Church by common consent confess that justification is taken in sacred Scripture in all these ways: nor does to be justified signify only either to acquire righteousness or to grow in righteousness: but frequently also to be declared or acknowledged just. This is to be seen in Becanus the Jesuit in Summa Theol. tom. 2 tract. 4 cap. 3 q. 1. To justify in sacred Scripture, he says, is used in three ways. First, so that it be the same as to make just, as Rom. 4:5. To him who believes in him who justifies the ungodly. Second, so that it be the same as to make more just, as James 2:24. You see that a man is justified by works, and not by faith only. And Apoc. 22:11. He that is just, let him be justified still. Third, so that it be the same as to declare or pronounce someone just, as Prov. 17:15. He who justifies the wicked, and he who condemns the just, both are abominable before God. Hence it comes about that justification also is taken in three ways: first for the acquisition of righteousness; second for the increase of righteousness; third for the declaration of righteousness.
pass_b_english: Roman consensus (Becanus): Scripture uses justify three ways—make just, make more just, declare just.
Justification likewise: acquisition, increase, or declaration of righteousness.

choices.why: Roman school maps all three Scriptural uses.
